summary: Agent fencing combines existing platform patterns into a single authority-and-history boundary.

items.text: Use named, structured review verdicts as the evidence consumed by escalation decisions.
Run work in sandboxed environments so the authority recorded by the platform matches the authority available at runtime.
Select model and execution channel separately; a trusted model through an unsuitable provider is still outside the fence.
Supply Trust Layer with platform-owned authority, action and artifact history; fencing establishes provenance, while the layer combines it with validation and review evidence.
Prevent retrieved content from expanding platform-owned authority: instruction-looking data may influence a proposal but cannot mint a grant.
Grant capabilities independently from the Agent–Computer Interface that describes operations, effects and evidence.
Write task, authority, tool and artifact history into a platform-owned run trace and expose a digest-bound evidence envelope for review.
See Context Compaction & JIT Retrieval for the related use case or counterpoint: Less context, retrieved on demand, beats more context dumped upfront.
See Council: Review Verdicts Need a Reaction for the related use case or counterpoint: Every named review finding gets an accountable decision: fix, accept with reasons, or escalate.

See Skip the Pull Request for the related use case or counterpoint: In agent-first delivery, gates in front of the integration merge replace the human pull-request review — the operator reads verdicts, not diffs.

See Switching Abstraction Layers for the related use case or counterpoint: Move from code and prompts to tasks, pipelines, reviews and capacity only when evidence makes the lower layer trustworthy enough to manage by signals.
